 Blog Hornbill Festival 2026: Dates, PAP Permit and Nagaland Guide
 The Hornbill Festival 2026 runs 1 to 10 December in Nagaland. Foreign visitors need a PAP permit. Dates, travel, stays and sourced budget ranges.
 October 23, 2026 
 17 min 
 Read article 
 Magazine 
 Table of Contents
 Loading... 
 Commercial partnership : This article contains affiliate links. If you book through these links, Pixidia earns a small commission at no extra cost to you.
 Learn more The Hornbill Festival 2026 runs from 1 to 10 December 2026 at Kisama, near Kohima, in Nagaland (India). If you are a foreign national, you need a Protected Area Permit (PAP), compulsory since 17 December 2024. You apply online on the e-FRRO portal before you arrive.
 Checked on 23 October 2026 against DD News and extracts from the Nagaland government websites; the circular is reported by the press, and the e-FRRO portal was not consulted directly. 
 The Hornbill Festival is the great celebration of Nagaland’s tribes, and most online guides skip the point that matters most: the permit. This article separates what is confirmed for 2026 from what is not, then walks you through what to sort out before you book a flight: permit, transport, accommodation, budget. The dates, figures and rules are sourced and dated 23 October 2026. The entry fee and the detailed programme were not published at that date: we don’t make them up.
 1. Dates, venue and what the festival stands for
 The festival opens on 1 December, the day of Nagaland’s state foundation day. The 27th edition is announced for 1 to 10 December 2026 by DD News (Prasar Bharati), which cites state government officials. The venue is Kisama Heritage Village, a living-museum village on a hill at the entrance to Kohima, the state capital.
 This is not an international tourist festival. In 2025, 214,493 people came in total, including 155,535 people from Nagaland and 56,431 Indians from other states: the published categories add up to 214,494, give or take one. Only 2,528 visitors were foreign. You will be a minority and an observer, and you will need to follow customs that were never written with visitors in mind.
 For the weather, the research gives only a qualitative indication: December is the cold season in the Kohima hills, and nights are cool. Pack warm layers for the mornings and evenings. No official average temperature has been recorded.
 The table below lists the published figures. No total exists yet for 2026.
 Hornbill Festival attendance, 2024 and 2025 Edition Total visitors Of which foreign Source 
 2024 (25th edition) 205,968 Not specified Eastern Mirror 
 2025 (26th edition) 214,493 2,528 Morung Express, 10 December 2025 
 2026 (27th edition) Not published Not published No source at the date of consultation 
 Source: Morung Express (2025) and Eastern Mirror (2024), checked on 23 October 2026. 
 2. Permits: the PAP is compulsory for foreigners
 This is the point most guides get wrong. A foreign national, whatever the reason for the trip, needs a Protected Area Permit (PAP) to enter Nagaland. The rule comes from circular no. 602 of the Ministry of Home Affairs, dated 17 December 2024. It was still in force at the date of consultation: the Nexplore guide, updated on 4 October 2026, describes it as compulsory. No relaxation had been announced for 2026 at that date. The one for 1 to 10 December 2025, reserved for tourism, expired on 10 December 2025.
 You apply online, on the e-FRRO portal (not consulted directly for this article). The 15 to 30 day window before arrival comes from a notice reported by the press in 2026, which we could not trace to the official source. Don’t assume you can get a permit on arrival: apply from home as soon as your dates are fixed.
 Permits required by traveller profile, as of 23 October 2026 Profile Permit Where to apply Stated lead time Status 
 Foreigner, any state Protected Area Permit (PAP) e-FRRO portal (indianfrro.gov.in) 15 to 30 days before arrival, stated in a press notice from 2026, not found at the official source Compulsory across Nagaland since 17 December 2024 
 Foreigner, long stay Registration with the FRO Local FRO office Within 24 hours, according to some guides Not confirmed by any official text we read 
 Indian from another state Inner Line Permit (ILP) ilp.nagaland.gov.in Online, in advance In force (notification of 14 August 2025) 
 Indian from Nagaland To be checked State authorities Not stated Check with the state authorities: no official source read 
 Source: MHA circular no. 602 of 17 December 2024, reported by Morung Express and NewsOnAir (24 February 2026); Nagaland ILP portal ; e-FRRO portal (link only, not consulted directly: the 15 to 30 day window comes from a press notice from 2026, not found at the official source). Checked on 23 October 2026. 
 Two points remain open. First, registration with the FRO within 24 hours of arrival is described by several guides, but we have not read any official text confirming it: check the portal before you leave. Second, the permit fee does not appear in any of the sources we checked.
 The political debate is heated. On 3 September 2026, the Nagaland Legislative Assembly voted unanimously to call on the Government of India to withdraw the PAP regime. The vote is not a decision. At the date of consultation the PAP is still compulsory, and that is the only rule to apply to your application.
 You will also read that the Dzükoü Valley is a must-see around the festival. Sources disagree on which permit it requires (PAP, ILP or another). We don’t recommend it in this guide until the rule is confirmed.
 3. Getting to Nagaland: Guwahati, Dimapur, Kohima
 The entry point is Dimapur airport (DMU). Flights to Dimapur run from Guwahati, Kolkata and Delhi, according to The Outdoor Backpacker (2026 guide). From Dimapur to Kohima, allow about 74 to 75 km along the NH-29, or 2.5 to 4 hours by road depending on traffic and weather. The Kohima to Kisama leg is shorter: sources give 12 to 18 km, and we have not settled between them.
 Photo by Vipin Joseph on Unsplash Dimapur, Kohima and Kisama
 Flight to Dimapur 
 74 to 75 km 
 2.5 to 4 h by road 
 1 to 10 December 2026 Kohima, the state capital, is where you book accommodation: hotels fill up several weeks ahead and, during the festival, the Kisama camps or nearby villages (section 5). During the festival, taxi fares rise sharply, according to a travel account published by Tripoto, without a verifiable figure. Arrange your transfer before you set off.
 Highlights
 A prepaid taxi at the airport avoids haggling. One unnamed source gives 2,500 to 3,500 rupees per trip to Kohima. 
 A shared taxi (sumo or Tata) is the cheapest option, but it only leaves once it is full. 
 Flights to Dimapur often connect through Guwahati, Kolkata or Delhi: compare routings for your dates. 
 Pixidia tip: book the airport transfer before you land, and keep your Kohima accommodation details on paper as well as on your phone. If your flight to Dimapur connects through Guwahati, the city can serve as a stopover. The card below is for the traveller in transit through Guwahati: a 120-minute walking tour of the Kamakhya temple and the Nilachal Hills, listed on Viator at €24.13 per person (price checked on 23 October 2026). Note: this tour does not go to Nagaland and does not replace the transport to Dimapur.
 Heritage walking tour of Kamakhya, in Guwahati 
 €24.13 per person (based on 2 adults, €48.26 for two), checked on 23 October 2026, available every day from 1 to 10 December 2026 · ★ 5.0 on Viator ( 2 reviews) 
See availability 
 Routes to Kohima and Kisama, as of 23 October 2026 Route Distance Stated duration Indicative cost 
 Dimapur airport to Kohima 74 to 75 km 2.5 to 4 h Prepaid taxi: 2,500 to 3,500 rupees (source not identified) 
 Kohima to Kisama 12 to 18 km depending on source Not stated Not stated 
 Guwahati to Dimapur Flight Varies by flight Not checked, depends on the date 
 Source: The Outdoor Backpacker (2026 guide), HappyFares (2026 guide), Tripoto (undated), cross-checked against guides. Checked on 23 October 2026. 
 4. Kisama Heritage Village and the tribes
 Photo by MOHAMED ABDUL RASHEED on Unsplash Kisama Heritage Village
 Kohima, Nagaland 
 Around fifteen tribes 
 1 to 10 December 2026 Kisama was designed to show the cultural diversity of Nagaland in one place. Each tribe has its own morung , the communal house for young men, which once passed on songs, rites, craftsmanship and the community’s rules. The state government presents the site on the page Naga Heritage Village on Tourism Nagaland .
 The number of tribes represented varies by source: 16 on the state tourism page, 17 on Wikipedia. Go with « around fifteen », and ask on site for the list of morungs to find out which communities are present this year.
 Highlights
 Dances, songs and traditional games performed by the communities themselves. Regional press describes the parades and traditional sports as the heart of the event. 
 Crafts and food at the stalls. The traditional dishes, according to the descriptions we read, are based on pork, fish, herbs and chillies. 
 An opening ceremony in the presence of state authorities. In 2025, the governor and the chief minister gave the start (IPR Nagaland). 
 Pixidia tip: always ask permission before photographing someone, especially dancers and craftspeople. Some sources mention a surcharge for professional cameras, with no amount or date verified. 5. Accommodation: book early, with no guaranteed rate
 Kohima fills up fast. The Outdoor Backpacker (2026 guide) advises booking four to six weeks ahead. Nexplore (updated 4 October 2026) talks about three to four months for hotels and homestays. Both lead times are given as advice, not rules: go with the longer one to be safe.
 During the festival, tent camps are set up at Kisama, and camps exist in nearby villages. A camp is not as comfortable as a hotel: ask what is provided (bed, hot water, toilets) before you pay.
 We do not publish any hotel or camp rate as certain. The price ranges in the guides are not verified: they are repeated, labelled as such, in section 6.
 Booking lead times given by guides, with no verified rates Accommodation type Location Stated lead time Source 
 Hotels and homestays Kohima 4 to 6 weeks ahead The Outdoor Backpacker, 2026 
 Hotels and homestays Kohima 3 to 4 months ahead Nexplore, updated 4 October 2026 
 Tent camps Kisama, 1 to 10 December Not stated The Outdoor Backpacker, 2026 
 Camps Villages near Kisama Not stated Several guides, no verified rates 
 Source: guides cited above, checked on 23 October 2026. No rate is given here because none was verified at that date. 
 6. Budget: the costs to work out before you go
 We do not give a verified budget. The estimates we found mix 2023 prices with unverified ranges. Here are the cost items to work through, in the order it makes most sense to handle them.
 The flight to Dimapur : the most variable item. It depends on your date and your connecting city (Guwahati, Kolkata or Delhi).
 The PAP permit : the fee is not listed in any source we checked. Read it on the e-FRRO portal.
 The Indian visa : the e-Visa is the usual route, but the amounts we found contradict each other. Check the official portal, indianvisaonline.gov.in.
 Transfers : the prepaid airport taxi, then local journeys, which cost more during the festival.
 Accommodation : ask hotels and camps for a quote for your exact dates.
 Meals : stalls and small eateries cover most needs. The table below gives an unverified order of magnitude.
 Entry : the 2026 fee is not published. See the section « What other guides don’t tell you » and the FAQ for the conflicting figures.
 Insurance : useful for a stay in India. See the section « Preparing your trip ».
 What it costs: unverified orders of magnitude
 These figures come from the research carried out on 23 October 2026. None has been confirmed on an official website: they are orders of magnitude, not a quote. Don’t treat them as a guaranteed price, and ask for a rate for your exact dates.
 Budget orders of magnitude, in Indian rupees (INR), unverified Item Order of magnitude Source and date Status 
 Budget hotel in Kohima, per night 2,000 to 4,500 INR HappyFares, 2026 guide Unverified 
 Mid-range hotel in Kohima, per night 5,500 to 12,000 INR HappyFares, 2026 guide Unverified 
 Tent camp at Kisama, per night (1 to 10 December) 3,500 to 8,500 INR HappyFares, 2026 guide Unverified 
 Prepaid airport taxi from Dimapur to Kohima, per trip 2,500 to 3,500 INR Source not identified Unverified 
 Average meal 300 INR TravelTrunk, January 2023 Old, unverified 
 Daily budget, budget travel (accommodation, meals, short transport; excluding flight and entry) 3,000 to 6,000 INR per day Research estimate, not a source Unsourced 
 Daily budget, mid-range travel (same items) 7,000 to 13,000 INR per day Research estimate, not a source Unsourced 
 Source: HappyFares (2026 guide), TravelTrunk (20 January 2023), source not identified for the taxi; research estimates for the daily budget. Data from the research of 23 October 2026; none has been confirmed on an official site. 
 To decide, start with accommodation quotes: that is the cost that dictates your dates. Once the room or camp is booked, choose the flight based on your arrival in Dimapur.
 7. A typical stay: arrive, settle in, see the festival
 The 2026 day-by-day programme is not published. The structure below is our own suggestion, not sourced: adjust it when the official schedule comes out.
 Day 1: arrival in Dimapur and transfer to Kohima. Don’t plan anything heavy: the drive takes several hours, and traffic varies.
 Days 2 to 4: Kisama. Spend these days at the living-museum village, the parades, dances and stalls. Leave early for the journey, as the 2026 opening time is not yet known. For Kisama, the research mentions a festival taxi or shuttle, not priced and with no specific source: ask your accommodation.
 Evenings: concerts and entertainment. The 2026 music line-up is not published. Don’t book concert tickets until it is.
 Days 5 to 10: the festival and the journey home. The festival runs until 10 December; no venue outside Kohima is documented to date. Book your return transfer as soon as you arrive.
 8. Depending on your profile
 First time in India. Getting to Nagaland already takes planning: permits, road, bookings. If you want to combine the festival with the north of the country, our North India 2026 guide covers Rajasthan, Delhi and Varanasi.
 Families. The festival takes place outdoors, with heavy local attendance. Sources don’t document facilities for children: check with the organisers before you go.
 Tight budget. Camps are an option. A shared taxi cuts the cost of the transfer, but it only leaves once full: expect to wait.
 Reduced mobility. Sources don’t describe the accessibility of the site or the roads. Ask your accommodation and the organisers before you book.
 Solo female travellers. We found no account published in 2026 that allows a conclusion. The verifiable advice is simple: book accommodation in advance, prepay the transfer, and share your itinerary with someone at home.
 9. Mistakes to avoid
 Going without a PAP and counting on the ILP. The Inner Line Permit applies to Indians coming from another state, not to foreigners.
 Assuming entry is free everywhere. One 2026 guide mentions a free day entry with a pass for a concert; others cite older amounts. Check on site.
 Treating hornbilfestival.com as an official site. It states itself that it is not linked to the Nagaland government.
 Booking accommodation at the last minute. Places in Kohima go several weeks ahead.
 Photographing without asking. People, especially dancers and craftspeople, expect to be asked.
 Relying on an old programme. Concerts and times change every year.
 What other guides don’t tell you
 Here are three points that the guides we read at the date of consultation leave out or get wrong.
 The most-cited 2026 guide mentions only the ILP, a mistake to avoid as a foreigner (section 2). The PAP rule is in MHA circular no. 602, reported by Morung Express (checked on 23 October 2026).
 The Nagaland Assembly vote of 3 September 2026 calls for scrapping the PAP. It is not a decision, and the PAP remains in force. The debate is reported by EastMojo (checked on 23 October 2026).
 The website hornbilfestival.com is not an official site. Its legal notice says so, and its 2026 dates are presented as « expected ». Several guides still cite it as a source ( dates page , checked on 23 October 2026).

 Frequently asked questions
 When is the Hornbill Festival 2026? The festival runs from 1 to 10 December 2026 at Kisama Heritage Village, near Kohima, in Nagaland. DD News published the date on 14 October 2026, citing state government officials, and the festival opens on state foundation day, 1 December. The date is announced, but the opening time and the detailed programme are not yet out.
 Do I need a permit for the Hornbill Festival? Yes, if you are a foreign national. The Protected Area Permit (PAP) has been compulsory across Nagaland since 17 December 2024 and is applied for online on the e-FRRO portal. An Indian from another state needs an Inner Line Permit (ILP), applied for on the state government’s portal. These rules come from the Ministry of Home Affairs circular, reported by the press in 2026.
 How far ahead should I apply for the PAP? A window of 15 to 30 days before arrival is given by a press notice from 2026, which we could not trace to the official source. Allow a margin: the research does not say how many days a correction to your application can take. Apply from home as soon as your dates are fixed, then keep a copy of the permit for the check on arrival.
 How much does the entry ticket cost? The official 2026 fee had not been published at the date of consultation. The amounts we found range from a free day entry, according to Nexplore (2026), which also mentions a pass for the evening concert, to 50 to 100 rupees per day, according to TravelTrunk (2023) and Thrillophilia (2025). Check with Tourism Nagaland or on site before you pay.
 Where should I stay during the festival? In Kohima, hotels are booked several weeks ahead: four to six weeks according to The Outdoor Backpacker, three to four months according to Nexplore. Tent camps are set up at Kisama during the festival. No rate is verified at the date of consultation; section 6 gives unverified orders of magnitude. Ask for a quote for your exact dates.
 How do I get from Dimapur to Kohima? The journey is about 74 to 75 km along the NH-29, or 2.5 to 4 hours by road depending on traffic and weather. The prepaid airport taxi is the simplest option. A shared taxi costs less, but it only leaves when it is full. Book the transfer before you arrive.
 How many tribes are represented at Kisama? Each tribe has its own morung at the Kisama village. The count varies by source: 16 on the state tourism page, 17 on Wikipedia. Go with around fifteen tribes, and ask on site for the list of communities present this year.
 Is it safe to go to the festival? We found no alert linked to the festival in 2026 in the sources we checked. That does not replace your home country’s travel advice, which we have not reviewed for Nagaland: check it before you go. Also ask your Kohima accommodation which roads it recommends before the transfer to Kisama, and follow its advice on site.
 Does the Assembly vote change anything for my ticket? No, not at the date of consultation. On 3 September 2026, the Nagaland Legislative Assembly voted a call on the Government of India to withdraw the PAP regime. The vote is not a decision: the PAP is still compulsory, and that is the rule to apply to your application.
 Sources
 DD News (Prasar Bharati) : 2026 dates and 27th edition, article of 14 October 2026.
 Morung Express : PAP rule for foreigners, reported in February 2026.
 Morung Express : 2025 attendance (214,493 visitors, including 2,528 foreigners).
 Tourism Nagaland, Naga Heritage Village : presentation of the site and count of morungs.
 Nagaland ILP portal : application for Indians from another state.
 e-FRRO portal : PAP application for foreigners (link only, not consulted directly for this article).
 EastMojo : Nagaland Assembly vote, 4 September 2026.
 The Outdoor Backpacker : 2026 guide, booking lead times and flights to Dimapur.
 Nexplore : guide updated 4 October 2026, PAP and entry.
 Wikipedia (EN) : festival overview and count of tribes.
 hornbilfestival.com : unofficial site, cited for its legal notice only.
 HappyFares : 2026 Hornbill guide, budget table (accommodation, camps) and taxi, checked on 23 October 2026.
 TravelTrunk : guide of 20 January 2023, meals and entry.
 Tripoto : travel account, undated (festival taxis, budget).
 Thrillophilia : 2025 listing, entry fee.
 Eastern Mirror (regional press, 2024): 2024 attendance, 205,968 visitors.
 NewsOnAir (public radio, 24 February 2026): PAP rule for foreigners, reported.
 Research carried out on 23 October 2026. Not all official portals were consulted directly. Permit rules and amounts change: confirm the procedures on the official portals before you leave.
